original_value: With the popularity of smart wearable systems, sensor signal processing poses more challenges to machine learning in embedded scenarios. For example, traditional machine-learning methods for data classification, especially in real time, are computationally intensive. The deployment of Artificial Intelligence algorithms on embedded hardware for fast data classification and accurate fall detection poses a huge challenge in achieving power-efficient embedded systems. Therefore, by exploiting the associative memory feature of Hopfield Neural Network, a hardware module has been designed to simulate the Neural Network algorithm which uses sensor data integration and data classification for recognizing the fall. By adopting the Hebbian learning method for training neural networks, weights of human activity features are obtained and implemented/embedded into the hardware design. Here, the neural network weight of fall activity is achieved through data preprocessing, and then the weight is mapped to the amplification factor setting in the hardware. The designs are checked with validation scenarios, and the experiment is completed with a Hopfield neural network in the analog module. Through simulations, the classification accuracy of the fall data reached 88.9% which compares well with some other results achieved by the software-based machine-learning algorithms, which verify the feasibility of our hardware design. The designed system performs the complex signal calculations of the hardware’s feedback signal, replacing the software-based method. A straightforward circuit design is used to meet the weight setting from the Hopfield neural network, which is maximizing the reusability and flexibility of the circuit design.

result.paraphrase: As smart wearable systems become more popular, sensor signal processing presents greater challenges for machine learning in embedded settings. In particular, conventional machine-learning approaches for data classification, especially in real time, are computationally demanding. Implementing artificial intelligence algorithms on embedded hardware for fast classification and accurate fall detection is a major challenge in building power-efficient embedded systems. To address this, a hardware module was designed based on the associative-memory property of the Hopfield Neural Network, simulating a neural-network algorithm that integrates sensor data and classifies it to recognize falls. Using Hebbian learning to train the neural network, weights for human-activity features are derived and embedded in the hardware design. In this work, the fall-activity neural-network weight is obtained through data preprocessing and then mapped to the amplification-factor setting in the hardware. The designs are evaluated in validation scenarios, and the experiment is carried out with a Hopfield neural network in the analog module. Simulation results show that fall-data classification accuracy reached 88.9%, which compares favorably with results from some software-based machine-learning algorithms and confirms the feasibility of the hardware design. The proposed system handles the complex signal computations of the hardware feedback signal, replacing the software-based approach. A simple circuit design is adopted to satisfy the weight-setting requirements of the Hopfield neural network, maximizing circuit reusability and flexibility.
